continuity_scope: Single-story pass bound to the official Small Beer Press English excerpt of “The End of a Dynasty or The Natural History of Ferrets,” from Angélica Gorodischer's Kalpa Imperial as translated by Ursula K. Le Guin. This tale is treated as a separate framed account inside a multi-story cycle; it is not flattened with other Kalpa tales, Spanish editions, or adaptations.

coverage_rule: Five individual named or stable-title-designated dramatic characters and seven direct within-story relations in the official English story text. The unnamed storyteller frame, dynasties, offices, peoples, cities, empire, and generic guards/servants remain dimensions or context rather than characters.
omissions: All people and stories outside “The End of a Dynasty or The Natural History of Ferrets,” including any cross-tale identity or chronology claims.
The anonymous storyteller/frame voice, whose identity and reliability remain unspecified in this tale.
Generic guards, servants, teachers, nobles, soldiers, officials, and the unnamed rival of the Ninth Emperor.
Spanish-edition wording and name variants not present in this official English witness.
uncertainties: Kalpa Imperial is a story cycle with multiple storytellers and a repeatedly rising/falling nameless empire; this pass is not a unified-series continuity map.
Narrator attributions distinguish hearsay, legend, and history-book claims; they are not silently upgraded to omniscient fact.
Loo’Loö may not be his actual name, and the Ninth Emperor's personal name is deliberately unavailable in the story.

Gorodischer is an Argentine writer and this is Le Guin's English translation. The fictional empire is not reduced to a generic or automatic allegory of Argentina or Latin America; in the publisher-hosted interview, Gorodischer rejects a simple allegorical reading while noting the book was written during dictatorship and concerns power.

The story includes state ritual, political repression, public humiliation, threatened execution, war, betrayal accusations, attempted filicide, death, and bodily coercion; later reign details are spoilers.
evidence_basis: The official Small Beer Press English excerpt supplies the full selected story text and character-level evidence. The book record confirms the collection's eleven-chapter, multiple-storyteller structure and author/translator/edition context; the author interview supplies only the non-allegory/context caution.
